references.text: Repeats the prohibition against eating fat and blood, with the penalty of being cut off from the people for anyone who breaks this command.
Elaborates on the prohibition against eating blood, explaining that blood is the seat of life and given for atonement on the altar.
The first prohibition against eating blood, given to Noah after the flood, as the basis for the eternal statute.
Moses repeats the prohibition against eating blood; the blood must be poured out on the ground like water.
Explains that blood is life, and one must not eat life together with the meat.
Saul forbids the people to eat meat containing blood, as a practical application of this law.
Ezekiel mentions fat and blood in connection with temple service and the covenant.
The Jerusalem council requires Gentile Christians to abstain from blood, continuing the biblical prohibition.
The apostolic letter repeats the prohibition against blood as one of the necessary things for Gentile Christians to observe.
Paul is reminded of the decisions made at the Jerusalem council, including the prohibition against blood.
7:26 specifies the scope of the prohibition against blood that 3:17 establishes as an eternal statute.
17:12 expands and confirms the validity of the blood prohibition in 3:17 also for foreigners.
